title: Needs/provides typed morphism records — one token, two objects, told apart with receipts
not_consumed_by: process_gates/needs_provides_composition_audit.py — FX-1 does not read this file and is byte-untouched by CT-3; the typed-join gate asserts the non-reference mechanically every run

record_shape.key: a join key in FX-1's three exact token shapes (K1/K2/K3), minus CT-1's own closed vocabulary tokens, which name values and not objects
record_shape.dom: a CT-1 base-category object id (Source-Layer L1..L4, Carrier C1..C11 of lab/methods/gu-base-categories.md), a CT-1 declared-unknown marker (UNTYPED = M1, HOMONYM-AMBIGUOUS = M4), or a registered-homonym sense id HOM:<token>#<n> resolving in lab/process/homonym-register.yaml
record_shape.map_type: a CT-1 arrow label from the reference's gu-token-codomain block (section 3.3)
record_shape.source_file: the repository path the typing was read from

receipt.site: the join site this record types: LEDGER:<row-id>, FORK:<fork-id>, or FILE:<relpath>
receipt.rule: the deterministic extraction rule that produced dom/cod/map_type; the gate RE-APPLIES it every run and reds if it does not reproduce the recorded values
receipt.quote: a byte-exact excerpt of source_file that the rule read

laws.no_guessing: Where the text supports no typing, the record is UNTYPED or HOMONYM-AMBIGUOUS — never a plausible object. The CN-2 principle, carried: a declared unknown is compliance; a plausible token is a lie.
laws.no_discriminator_without_a_receipt: A homonym-sense discriminator may be recorded only for a kind:homonym register entry whose own disambiguator states it, every entry cites the register substrings that state it, and the gate re-measures byte-disjointness across the owning files on every run. This is the mirror of FX-1's alias law: FX-1's alias table MERGES two notations into one object; this table SPLITS one notation into two objects.
laws.no_dom_alias_without_a_receipt: dom_aliases is the typed analogue of FX-1's alias table and is EMPTY. An entry may be added only with a live receipt path plus the substring that proves the identification; the gate reds on a receipt-free entry.
laws.thirteenth_object: CT-3 coins no CT-1 object. HOM:<token>#<n> points at the homonym register, which CT-1 section 3.5 names as the disambiguation surface for registered tokens (a bare registered token fails to name an object). Every CT-1 category keeps its <= 12 object budget. A mixed LAYER (a+b) is recorded UNTYPED with its BRIDGE quoted, because CT-1 has no product object and CT-3 will not invent one.

R1_fx2_typed_object_blocks.description: ```gu-typed-objects blocks in the FX-2 gate's format; dom from a named CT-1 Carrier object occurring verbatim in the carrier slot, else from LAYER=; cod from a named Carrier object in the target slot; map_type from MAP-TYPE=. Conflicting blocks in one file give UNTYPED (fx2-block-conflict).
R1_fx2_typed_object_blocks.measured_at_mint: 22 blocks across 15 files when the extraction was first measured; 28 across 20 at close of build the same day (the frontier moves as sibling channels adopt the FX-2 block)

R2_ledger_context.description: CT-2's per-row `context` projection. CT-2 landed its schema on the same day (lab/process/conditional-physics-ledger-schema-v0.2.json, $defs.context: the required (layer, grant, carrier) triple, whose codomains are CT-1's own object ids -- L* for the Source-Layer axis, G* for the Grant poset, C* for the Carrier axis) and scoped the obligation to ledger version v0.260 ONWARD, deliberately not retro-filling existing ledgers. So this source is specified and still empty: the latest ledger lab/process/conditional-physics-ledger-v0.259.json carries no `context` key on any of its 87 rows. The gate re-measures that every run and reds if rows gain the field while this flag still reads false, which is the signal to re-mint these records against the new axis. The carrier slot's codomain is identical to this file's `dom` codomain, so no adapter is needed when it arrives.
R2_ledger_context.measured_at_mint: 0 of 87 rows in v0.259; schema for v0.260+ present as of CT-2, 2026-08-17

R3_prose_tokens.description: Explicit LAYER= / MAP-TYPE= tokens written in prose outside any fenced block.

R4_homonym_senses.description: Registered-homonym sense resolution. R4a (homonym-sense-by-owning-file) resolves a text that names exactly one sense's owning file — CP-1's own move, 'same object verified by LINEAGE RECEIPT, not token'. R4b (homonym-sense-by-discriminator) resolves a text carrying exactly one sense's byte-disjoint discriminator. Both-or-neither is HOMONYM-AMBIGUOUS.
R4_homonym_senses.measured_at_mint: 1 token with a receipted discriminator set (v_PSB), 2 refused; 13 records (5 by lineage receipt, 8 by discriminator)

receipts.note: The register's own disambiguator states both the naming rule and the byte-disjointness this table mechanises; the gate re-measures the disjointness against the two owning files every run rather than trusting the sentence.

sense_discriminators_refused.reason: The register's disambiguator is a rule for FUTURE WRITING ('name the signature (Riemannian Met vs Met_Lor/Y14), and bundle vs section space'), not a byte-disjoint substring that partitions the existing corpus; neither sense's locus supplies a token a census could read off an arbitrary file. Recording a discriminator here would be guessing, which the no-guessing law forbids. The FX-1 candidate pair FORK:NUMBER-14-METRIC-VS-EXTERIOR::Met(X^4) therefore stays TYPE-UNVERIFIED, honestly.
sense_discriminators_refused.register_must_contain: name the signature (Riemannian Met vs Met_Lor/Y14), and bundle vs section space

sense_discriminators_refused.reason: The register REFUSES sensing on this token itself ('not sensed: bare so(1,3) is correct in the hundreds of single-sense contexts ... which a token census cannot see'). CT-1 already carries the two SUBSCRIPTED forms as Carrier objects C8 (so(1,3)_endo) and C9 (so(1,3)_H), which rule R1's named-carrier branch reads directly; the BARE token remains a non-object, exactly as CT-1 section 3.5 says.
